applicant_profile: Pakistani nationals applying for a US F-1 student visa (Islamabad embassy / Karachi consulate).
framing_disclaimer: Measures DOCUMENTED READINESS and 214(b)/financial RISK EXPOSURE. Does NOT predict the consular officer's decision — 214(b) is subjective and interview-driven. Not legal advice. Verify SEVIS fee, social-media rule, and current vetting/appointment conditions at travel.state.gov and ice.gov before applying.

config.financial_basis: NO US government living-cost figure. Required funds = the TOTAL cost of attendance stated on the student's Form I-20 (tuition + living + fees) for the first academic year, plus return travel and a sensible buffer.
config.english_test_basis: US visa itself does NOT mandate a standalone English test; the SEVP school sets admission English requirements. Do not treat a missing IELTS/PTE as a visa blocker.
config.social_media_rule: From 18 Jun 2025, F/M/J applicants must set ALL social media profiles to public and disclose every handle used in the last 5 years on DS-160. No official pre-interview deadline specified; keep profiles public until a decision is made.
config.passport_validity_rule: Pakistani passport valid at least 6 months beyond intended US stay.
config.entry_window: New/initial F-1 students cannot enter the US more than 30 days before the I-20 program start date.
config.section_214b: INA 214(b): every nonimmigrant applicant is presumed an intending immigrant and must overcome it. #1 F-1 refusal ground for Pakistani applicants. Inherently officer-subjective and interview-driven.
config.note: US student-visa policy is changing rapidly in 2025-2026 (EO 14161 vetting expansions). Re-verify SEVIS fee, social-media rule, and interview/appointment conditions at travel.state.gov and ice.gov before each production cycle.

score_bands.label: Low Risk — Appears Well-Prepared for Interview
score_bands.description: Well-prepared file with low visible 214(b)/financial risk. NOT a prediction — F-1 approval is officer-subjective and interview-driven. Re-verify fees/policy and prepare your interview answers.

score_bands.label: Moderate 214(b) Risk — Improve Before Interview
score_bands.description: Eligible but with weak points an officer will probe (ties, funding story, study-plan logic, consistency). Close flagged items and rehearse before the interview.

score_bands.label: High Refusal Risk
score_bands.description: Serious unresolved gaps. Attending the interview now with these issues unaddressed indicates high 214(b) risk and document readiness shortfalls. Resolve all high-risk flags before proceeding.

score_bands.label: Critical Refusal Risk
score_bands.description: Critical mandatory items are missing or integrity flags are present. Do not attend yet — these unresolved issues are serious refusal-ground risks, and misrepresentation/concealment risks a permanent bar.

tiers.hard_blocker: Any triggered hard blocker forces 'Critical Refusal Risk'; score skipped. Mandatory items (SEVP/I-20/SEVIS/DS-160/passport/social-media/funds/full-time/work-auth/disclosure/no-fake-docs) or core 214(b) failure.
tiers.high_risk_flag: Each triggered high-risk flag deducts impact AND caps the max band: 1-2 => 'High Refusal Risk'; 3+ => 'Critical Refusal Risk'. Prevents averaging from hiding serious 214(b)/financial risk.
tiers.soft_warning: Each triggered soft warning deducts impact within band; does not cap the band.

calculation_logic.step_1: Evaluate hard blockers. If ANY triggers -> 'Critical Refusal Risk'; stop.
calculation_logic.step_2: Per category: category_score = (sum score_impact of PASSING scored questions / sum score_impact of ALL scored questions) x max_points. 'info' questions (trigger_if=never) are routing-only.
calculation_logic.step_3: total_score = sum of category scores, rounded to nearest integer.
calculation_logic.step_4: Count triggered high-risk flags; apply band cap (1-2 => High; 3+ => Critical).
calculation_logic.step_5: Map total to a band; final band = worse of score-band and cap-band.
calculation_logic.passing_definition: A question PASSES when the answer satisfies pass_if. Financial pass requires funds covering the full I-20 cost-of-attendance + travel (no fixed US figure).
calculation_logic.rounding: Category to 1 decimal; total to nearest integer.

result_payload_template.label: <band label>
result_payload_template.estimated_refusal_concerns: <triggered hard blockers + high-risk flags in plain English>
result_payload_template.recommended_improvements: <soft warnings + how to close each flag>
result_payload_template.priority_action_list: <hard blockers first, then high-risk flags, then soft warnings>
result_payload_template.interview_preparation_advice: <rehearse why-USA/this-school, funding/source-of-funds in own words, return plan, refusal explanation>
result_payload_template.financial_documentation_advice: <6-month statements, sponsor FBR/NTN/salary proof, documented source for every major deposit, full-program funding>
result_payload_template.ds160_i20_sevis_consistency_warning: <reconcile name/funding/program/dates across DS-160, I-20, SEVIS receipt, admission letter, financials>
result_payload_template.risk_explanation: <why this band, referencing 214(b) and interview subjectivity>
result_payload_template.disclaimer: Readiness assessment, not an approval prediction or legal advice. Verify all fees/policies at travel.state.gov and ice.gov before applying.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: Must Be Accepted at an SEVP-Certified School
critical_blockers_hard.message: Only SEVP-certified schools can issue an I-20. Verify the school yourself — agents sometimes push non-SEVP or low-credibility schools that wreck your 214(b) case.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: Form I-20 Mandatory — Must Be Signed and Current
critical_blockers_hard.message: The I-20 (Certificate of Eligibility) is issued by the school's DSO after you're entered in SEVIS. No I-20 = no F-1 application.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: Form I-20 Mandatory — Must Be Signed and Current
critical_blockers_hard.message: An unsigned I-20 is invalid. Sign it and confirm the DSO signature is present.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: Form I-20 Mandatory — Must Be Signed and Current
critical_blockers_hard.message: For your first US entry the school on the visa must match the I-20. If you change schools before the visa, get an updated visa.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: SEVIS I-901 Fee Must Be Paid Before Visa Is Issued
critical_blockers_hard.message: The SEVIS fee (USD 350 for F-1) must be paid BEFORE the visa is issued. Pay only at fmjfee.com — beware fake payment sites pushed by agents. No paid fee on record = refusal on the day, no same-day fix.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: SEVIS I-901 Fee Must Be Paid Before Visa Is Issued
critical_blockers_hard.message: Pay using the exact SEVIS ID on your I-20. A mismatch means the system can't confirm your payment at the interview.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: DS-160 Online Application Must Be Completed and Consistent
critical_blockers_hard.message: The DS-160 is mandatory before the interview. Complete it carefully — it is the spine of your case and everything you say at interview must match it.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: DS-160 Online Application Must Be Completed and Consistent
critical_blockers_hard.message: Bring the printed DS-160 confirmation barcode page to the interview. Without it you can be turned away.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: Social Media Must Be Public and Fully Disclosed (From June 18, 2025)
critical_blockers_hard.message: List every platform/handle from the last 5 years, including inactive ones. Omitting an account is a ground for denial and a possible bar.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: Social Media Must Be Public and Fully Disclosed (From June 18, 2025)
critical_blockers_hard.message: Since 18 Jun 2025, F/M/J applicants must make all profiles public for vetting. No official deadline is specified, so set them public before submitting and keep them public until a decision is made.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: Non-Immigrant Intent Must Be Demonstrated — Section 214(b)
critical_blockers_hard.message: 214(b) is the #1 refusal ground for Pakistani F-1 applicants. The officer PRESUMES you intend to immigrate; you must overcome it with a credible, specific return story — in seconds, verbally.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: Visa Interview at US Embassy/Consulate Required
critical_blockers_hard.message: An interview is required for most applicants 14-79. Book early; wait times vary. 2025-2026 vetting can add 221(g) administrative processing.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: Visa Interview at US Embassy/Consulate Required
critical_blockers_hard.message: Assemble the full set before the day. Missing a core document can end the interview before it starts.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20
critical_blockers_hard.message: The US sets no fixed figure — you must cover the total cost of attendance stated on YOUR I-20, plus return travel, without unauthorized work. Underfunding is a top 214(b) refusal cause.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: Prior Visa Refusals and Immigration Violations Must Be Disclosed
critical_blockers_hard.message: Failing to disclose a prior refusal or violation on DS-160 is misrepresentation — a permanent-bar risk far worse than the refusal itself.

critical_blockers_hard.mapped_rule: Passport Must Be Valid 6+ Months Beyond Intended Stay
critical_blockers_hard.message: Renew before applying if needed. An insufficiently valid passport blocks visa issuance.
Fabricated bank balances, fake experience letters, or altered transcripts cause refusal AND a permanent misrepresentation bar — even if an agent did it in your name. Verify every document.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Form I-20 Mandatory — Must Be Signed and Current
high_risk_flags.message: Mismatches between the I-20, DS-160, admission letter, and financial papers are a classic Pakistani refusal trigger. Cross-check name spelling, funding amount, program, and dates.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: DS-160 Online Application Must Be Completed and Consistent
high_risk_flags.message: Agents sometimes enter wrong job titles, hide refusals, or inflate funding on your DS-160. You are bound by what's submitted in your name — and asked about it under oath. Read every field yourself.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: DS-160 Online Application Must Be Completed and Consistent
high_risk_flags.message: Inconsistency between DS-160 and your documents reads as misrepresentation. Reconcile funding figures, employment, education dates, and family details before submitting.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Non-Immigrant Intent Must Be Demonstrated — Section 214(b)
high_risk_flags.message: No ties = near-certain 214(b) refusal. Strongest ties are concrete: property in your name, a family business, a written career/job plan in Pakistan, assets. 'Parents live here' alone is weak.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Non-Immigrant Intent Must Be Demonstrated — Section 214(b)
high_risk_flags.message: Generic answers sink interviews. Name the program, faculty, or specialization and tie it to your background and a Pakistan-based career. A random/agent-picked university is a 214(b) red flag.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Non-Immigrant Intent Must Be Demonstrated — Section 214(b)
high_risk_flags.message: Show the path: your background -> this US program -> a named role/sector in Pakistan. No logical payoff at home signals immigration intent.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Interview Readiness — Consistent, Genuine, Unscripted Answers
high_risk_flags.message: Officers test whether YOU understand who pays and how they earned it. 'My uncle handles it' is weak. Know your sponsor's job, business, and how the money was accumulated.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Interview Readiness — Consistent, Genuine, Unscripted Answers
high_risk_flags.message: Officers spot rehearsed agent scripts instantly and it hurts credibility. Practise the content, but answer in your own words.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20
high_risk_flags.message: No documents = automatic financial credibility failure. Bring bank statements (6 months), sponsor income proof, FBR returns, and source-of-funds evidence.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20
high_risk_flags.message: A balance that appears suddenly before applying signals arranged funds. Consistent history over months is far stronger.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20
high_risk_flags.message: Each major deposit needs proof: registered sale deed (property), FBR-declared salary, sanctioned loan letter, or a notarised gift affidavit from a traceable giver.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20
high_risk_flags.message: A sponsor showing big funds but non-filer/no FBR history is a major red flag — it implies undeclared income. Declared income should plausibly support the amount.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20
high_risk_flags.message: Verbal claims aren't enough. Salary slips, business registration/NTN, FBR returns, and matching bank inflows make a sponsor credible.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Educational Consistency and Study-Plan Logic (214(b)-linked)
high_risk_flags.message: Provide employment letters, salary slips, freelance proof, or transcripts covering the gap. Unevidenced 'I was at home/preparing' is weak and invites doubt at interview.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Educational Consistency and Study-Plan Logic (214(b)-linked)
high_risk_flags.message: A big, unexplained field switch (e.g. completed Bachelors then an unrelated junior program) is a 214(b) trigger. If yes, be ready to explain the logic credibly.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Educational Consistency and Study-Plan Logic (214(b)-linked)
high_risk_flags.message: Officers question progression that doesn't add up — e.g. a Masters-holder enrolling in a lower diploma. A downgrade looks like a visa-shopping move.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Educational Consistency and Study-Plan Logic (214(b)-linked)
high_risk_flags.message: Inconsistent or unverifiable academics (mismatched names/dates, missing transcripts) raise fraud concerns. Have complete, attested records ready.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Prior Visa Refusals and Immigration Violations Must Be Disclosed
high_risk_flags.message: Prior refusals are visible and probed. A refusal is survivable IF disclosed and explained — concealment on DS-160 is misrepresentation with a permanent-bar risk.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Prior Visa Refusals and Immigration Violations Must Be Disclosed
high_risk_flags.message: Overstays/removals strongly conflict with 'genuine temporary student' and must be disclosed and addressed candidly.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Prior Visa Refusals and Immigration Violations Must Be Disclosed
high_risk_flags.message: An asylum history conflicts with intent to return and must be addressed candidly, ideally with legal advice.

high_risk_flags.mapped_rule: Application Integrity and Agent Risk
high_risk_flags.message: If an agent told you to conceal something, that is a path to a misrepresentation bar. Disclose truthfully; drop the agent's advice.

soft_warnings.mapped_rule: Social Media Must Be Public and Fully Disclosed (From June 18, 2025)
soft_warnings.message: Officers may review your public presence. This is about safety/security risk and consistency with your application — not ordinary opinions. Check for content contradicting your study/return story.

soft_warnings.mapped_rule: Non-Immigrant Intent Must Be Demonstrated — Section 214(b)
soft_warnings.message: Vague 'I'll find a good job' is weak. Have a concrete plan: target employer/sector, family business role, or further step in Pakistan.

soft_warnings.mapped_rule: Interview Readiness — Consistent, Genuine, Unscripted Answers
soft_warnings.message: Don't hide or over-explain a past refusal. State what changed since then (stronger ties/finances/clearer plan).

soft_warnings.mapped_rule: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20
soft_warnings.message: Immediate-family sponsorship (father, mother, brother) is expected. Uncle/aunt/grandfather or 'family friend' sponsors raise scrutiny and need a strong relationship + funds explanation.

soft_warnings.mapped_rule: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20
soft_warnings.message: Funding that barely covers year one with no plan for later years is a 214(b) concern. Show how the whole program is covered.

soft_warnings.mapped_rule: Cannot Enter the US More Than 30 Days Before Program Start
soft_warnings.message: New F-1 students arriving earlier than 30 days before the start date are denied entry. Plan travel accordingly.
Dropping below full-time without DSO approval terminates status. Understand this before you go.

soft_warnings.mapped_rule: No Work Without Proper Authorization — Zero Tolerance
soft_warnings.message: Unauthorized work permanently terminates F-1 status and risks deportation and future bars. On-campus/CPT/OPT have specific rules.

soft_warnings.mapped_rule: F-2 Dependants Cannot Work Under Any Circumstances
soft_warnings.message: F-2 dependants are absolutely barred from working. Violation ends F-2 status. (F-2 funds also add to what you must show.)
